headline: Money is a tool for exchange—a medium that stores and transfers value between people and across time
universal_truth: Money is a social agreement; it works because everyone agrees it has value
fun_facts: Money has taken many forms: shells, beads, salt, metals, paper, and now digital records
Money serves three functions: medium of exchange, store of value, unit of account
Hyperinflation shows what happens when money loses trust—it becomes worthless paper
discussion_questions: How does your relationship with money affect your life?
What can money buy and what can't it buy?

hook.title: Welcome
hook.script: Paper with numbers. Digital records in databases. Why does money have value? Not because of what it's made of, but because everyone agrees it does. Money is a social technology—a shared belief that enables exchange.

options.text: I want to learn something new
options.response: Perfect. Curiosity is the first step to understanding. Let's explore this together.
That curiosity is exactly what we need. Let's dive in and discover something amazing.

cliff.title: The Question
cliff.script: Money isn't inherently valuable—you can't eat it or wear it. So what makes it work?

options.text: Money works through collective agreement—everyone accepts it because everyone else accepts it; this shared belief creates real value; money is a coordination tool based on trust
options.response: Yes. Money is a shared story we all believe. The paper is worthless; the agreement gives it value. This makes money fragile—if trust breaks, money breaks—but also powerful.
Government backing is one trust mechanism, but ultimately money requires people to accept it...

q1.title: Exchange Medium
q1.script: Money solves the 'double coincidence of wants'—needing someone who has what you want AND wants what you have. With money, you can sell to anyone, buy from anyone. This enables complex economies.
q1.prompt: What's your first impression of "Exchange Medium"?

options.text: This confirms what I already knew
options.response: Great foundation! Now let's build on that knowledge with something you might not expect...
Perfect starting point! This insight will connect to even more surprising facts ahead.

q2.title: Value Storage
q2.script: Money stores value across time. You work today, spend next year. This time-shifting requires money to hold value—which is why inflation matters. Money that loses value fails as storage.
q2.prompt: How does this connect to what you already know?

options.response: Exactly. These connections are how knowledge becomes understanding.

options.text: I need to think about this more
options.response: That's a good instinct. Deep understanding takes time. The next fact will help clarify.

q3.title: Beyond Money
q3.script: Money measures some value but not all. Health, relationships, purpose—these matter but aren't priced. Don't confuse what money can measure with what matters. Some valuable things aren't for sale.
q3.prompt: What surprises you most about this?

options.text: I never thought about it this way
options.response: That shift in perspective is exactly the point. New angles reveal new truths.
That's learning in action. When understanding shifts, you're really getting it.

wisdom.title: Today's Wisdom
wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: Money is a social agreement. It works because everyone agrees it has value. Understand this tool without worshipping it.
wisdom.prompt: What resonates most with you today?

options.response: That central truth will stay with you. Let it guide your thinking.
Application is where knowledge becomes wisdom. That's the real learning.

outro.title: See You Tomorrow
outro.script: That's Day 338. Tomorrow, we'll explore exchanging what you have—barter and negotiation. Until then, consider your relationship with money.
outro.prompt: Before you go—what will you take from today?

options.response: Reflection deepens learning. Let these ideas simmer in your mind.
Teaching others is the best way to learn. You've already begun the ripple.

growTrack.title: Money Reflection - What's Your Relationship?
growTrack.activity: What's your relationship with money—anxiety, comfort, scarcity, abundance? How does money affect your decisions? What would a healthier relationship with money look like? What can't money buy that matters to you?
